findings.title: Smooth on a list of datasets smooths ACROSS dataset boundaries, silently mixing subjects' data
findings.description: hyp.manip(list_of_datasets, model='Smooth') is documented as a per-dataset operation (manip.py docstring: 'Apply a per-dataset manipulation'; docs/pipeline_order.rst: 'Manip runs in native (per-dataset) space ... per-dataset preprocessing steps (e.g. denoising a single subject's timeseries)'). In reality Smooth's _transform_stacked is decorated with dw.decorate.apply_stacked, which concatenates the list into one stacked DataFrame BEFORE the savgol/gaussian/boxcar filter runs, so the filter treats all subjects as one continuous timeseries. Each dataset's edge samples are contaminated by the neighboring dataset (about kernel_width/2 samples on each side of every boundary). Probe: subject A = all zeros, subject B = all ones, kernel_width=11: A's last samples become up to 0.396 and B's first samples drop to 0.604. This silently corrupts the canonical multi-subject workflow (e.g. smoothing the 36-subject 'weights' dataset, exactly what the gallery recipes do). By contrast Resample's transformer explicitly recurses per-dataset, and ZScore/Normalize sharing fit stats across the list is at least documented in their fitters -- Smooth's cross-boundary filtering is documented nowhere and contradicts the docs. Affects all three kernels (verified for savgol and gaussian).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
a = np.zeros((30, 2)); b = np.ones((30, 2))
sm = hyp.manip([a, b], model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, maintain_bounds=False)
print(np.asarray(sm[0], dtype=float)[-3:, 0])  # expected [0. 0. 0.]
print(np.asarray(sm[1], dtype=float)[:3, 0])   # expected [1. 1. 1.]
findings.expected: Each dataset smoothed independently: sm[0] stays all zeros, sm[1] stays all ones (a constant signal is invariant under smoothing).
findings.actual:
ds0 unchanged (all 0): False  ds0 tail: [0.03962704 0.2004662  0.3962704 ]
ds1 unchanged (all 1): False  ds1 head: [0.6037296  0.7995338  0.96037296]
gaussian ds0 all 0: False ds1 all 1: False

findings.title: Resample axis=1 crashes with DTypePromotionError on any DataFrame with string column names
findings.description: Resample's documented axis=1 ('1 to resample along columns instead (transposed internally)') transposes the DataFrame and then uses the transposed index -- i.e. the ORIGINAL COLUMN LABELS -- as the interpolation x-axis. With the near-universal case of string-named columns, np.linspace/pchip over string labels raises a cryptic numpy DTypePromotionError. It only works when column labels happen to be numeric (e.g. array input wrangled to integer labels: (4,20) int-labeled frame -> (4,9) fine).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3), columns=list('abc'))
hyp.manip(df, model='Resample', axis=1, n_samples=9)
findings.expected: Either resample each row over column positions (documented behavior), or a clear error explaining that axis=1 requires numeric column labels.
findings.actual: DTypePromotionError: The DType <class 'numpy.dtypes._PyFloatDType'> could not be promoted by <class 'numpy.dtypes.StrDType'>. This means that no common DType exists for the given inputs. For example they cannot be stored in a single array un...

findings.title: Fitted Smooth cannot be reused on data with different column labels: bare KeyError (ZScore/Normalize got the positional-keying fix, Smooth did not)
findings.description: QC 2026-07 fixed ZScore and Normalize to key fitted per-column params POSITIONALLY so a model fitted on an ndarray (integer labels) can be reused on a named DataFrame. Smooth's maintain_bounds clip lookup (smooth.py _transform_stacked: kwargs['min'][c] / kwargs['max'][c]) is still LABEL-keyed, so the exact scenario that motivated the QC fix crashes for Smooth with a bare KeyError. There is also no column-count guard: reusing on a frame with a different number of columns raises KeyError('w') instead of ZScore's clear 'was fit on 3 column(s) but got 4'. Verified that the identical scenario works for ZScore.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.randn(40, 3)
_, ms = hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, return_model=True)
newdf = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(40, 3), columns=['roi1', 'roi2', 'roi3'])
hyp.manip(newdf, model=ms)
findings.expected: Smoothed (40,3) output, matching ZScore's behavior in the identical scenario ('ZScore fit-on-array->reuse-on-nameddf: OK (40, 3)').
findings.actual:
KeyError: 'roi1'   (with 3 differently-named cols)
KeyError: 'w'      (with 4 cols; no count guard)

findings.title: Fitted Smooth reuse replays FIT-TIME min/max bounds onto new data, silently clipping it to the old range
findings.description: maintain_bounds exists to suppress filter overshoot relative to the INPUT's range, but on the documented return_model reuse path the fit-time per-column min/max are replayed onto new data. New data outside the fit-time range is silently flattened to the old bounds: data centered at 100 came back entirely within [1.05, 2.24] (each value pinned at its column's fit-time max). 100% of values corrupted, no warning. This is the same 'replay fit-time state that should be data-derived' bug class that round17 fixed for Resample (its transformer now derives x from the data being transformed). Workaround: maintain_bounds=False.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
df = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(size=(40, 3)), columns=list('abc'))
_, ms = hyp.manip(df, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11, return_model=True)
new = pd.DataFrame(rng.normal(loc=100.0, size=(30, 3)), columns=list('abc'))
out = hyp.manip(new, model=ms)
print(np.asarray(out, dtype=float).min(), np.asarray(out, dtype=float).max())
findings.expected: Smoothed values near 100 (clipping, if any, relative to the transformed data's own pre-smoothing range).
findings.actual: out range=[1.05,2.24] on input centered at 100 -- every output value equals its column's fit-time maximum.

findings.title: pandas Series input to manip() is wrangled to an EMPTY (0,0) DataFrame, then fails with nonsense errors
findings.description: dw.wrangle(pd.Series(...)) returns an empty (0, 0) DataFrame (datawrangler upstream behavior), so hyp.manip(series, ...) fails downstream with errors that have nothing to do with the real problem: ZScore raises 'IndexError: list index out of range', Smooth raises 'kernel_width (11) is larger than the number of samples (0); use a kernel_width <= 0.' -- actively misleading, since the user's Series had 40 samples. Passing a single column (df['col']) is one of the most common things a scientist does. hyp.normalize(series) meanwhile works correctly, returning a (40, 1) array. Root cause is upstream (datawrangler funnel), but manip is the exposed surface; a type check or a Series->to_frame() coercion at the funnel boundary would fix it. [infra note: upstream package is pydata-wrangler, installed in the repo venv; not modified per audit rules]
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
s = pd.Series(np.sin(np.linspace(0, 6, 40)), name='sig')
hyp.manip(s, model='ZScore')
findings.expected: Treat the Series as a (40,1) dataset (as hyp.normalize does), or raise a clear 'unsupported type' error naming Series and the fix.
findings.actual:
dw.wrangle(Series) -> DataFrame (0, 0)
manip(Series, ZScore) -> IndexError: list index out of range
manip(Series, Smooth) -> ValueError: kernel_width (11) is larger than the number of samples (0); use a kernel_width <= 0.

findings.title: manip ZScore returns all-NaN for single-row (and 1-D) input; hyp.normalize returns zeros for the same input
findings.description: ZScore's fitter uses pandas .std() (ddof=1), which is NaN for a single observation; the QC zero-variance guard (std_safe = np.where(std == 0, 1.0, std)) does not catch NaN, so every output value is silently NaN. tools.normalize's _zscore_column guard returns zeros for the same degenerate input (as does sklearn's StandardScaler). Compounding it, a 1-D array is wrangled by the funnel as a single ROW (1,n) -- so hyp.manip(np.array([1,2,3,4]), 'ZScore') silently returns [[nan nan nan nan]], while hyp.normalize treats 1-D input as a column (4,1) and z-scores it correctly.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.manip(np.array([1., 2., 3., 4.]), model='ZScore'))
print(hyp.normalize(np.array([1., 2., 3., 4.])))
findings.expected: Either zeros (matching hyp.normalize/sklearn convention) or a clear error; not silent NaN. 1-D orientation consistent between the two APIs.
findings.actual:
E5.manip-1d -> (1, 4) [nan nan nan nan]
E5.normalize-1d -> (4, 1) [-1.34164079 -0.4472136   0.4472136   1.34164079]
E3.manip-zscore-single-row values=[[nan nan nan]]

findings.title: manip() empty/None input errors are cryptic; empty LIST takes the text path and loads a topic-model corpus
findings.description: hyp.normalize gives a model error message for degenerate input ('input has no observations (0 rows); there is nothing to plot or analyze.'). hyp.manip on the same inputs: empty DataFrame, empty (0,3) array, and None all raise bare 'IndexError: list index out of range'; an empty list [] is interpreted by the funnel as TEXT, prints 'loading corpus: minipedia...done!' (corpus load side effect) and then fails inside sklearn LDA with 'Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.'
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(), model='ZScore')   # IndexError
# hyp.manip([], model='ZScore')             # corpus load + LDA ValueError
# hyp.manip(None, model='ZScore')           # IndexError
findings.expected: A clear 'input has no observations' / 'unsupported input' error like hyp.normalize's, without loading text corpora.
findings.actual:
IndexError: list index out of range
loading corpus: minipedia...done! ValueError: Found array with 0 sample(s) (shape=(0, 1220)) while a minimum of 1 is required by LatentDirichletAllocation.

findings.title: Smooth's non-integer kernel_width warning says 'Rounding ... to the nearest integer' but the code truncates
findings.description: smooth.py transformer: the warning fires when kernel_width != round(kernel_width), but the assignment is kwargs['kernel_width'] = int(kwargs['kernel_width']) -- truncation. kernel_width=11.7 warns 'Rounding smoothing kernel width to the nearest integer' then uses width 11 (verified byte-identical to savgol_filter(x, 11, 3)); actual rounding would give 12, then the odd-bump would make it 13.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
from scipy.signal import savgol_filter
long = pd.DataFrame({'y': np.arange(50.)})
r = hyp.manip(long, model='Smooth', kernel_width=11.7, maintain_bounds=False)
print(np.allclose(np.asarray(r['y'], dtype=float), savgol_filter(np.arange(50.), 11, 3)))  # True -> truncated
findings.expected: Behavior matches the warning: 11.7 -> 12 -> (odd bump) 13; or the warning says 'Truncating'.
findings.actual: warnings: ['Rounding smoothing kernel width to the nearest integer']; effective width used: 11

findings.title: Documented ValueError cases actually raise AssertionError (stripped under python -O), and normalize's message names a nonexistent 'scale_type' parameter
findings.description: Three separate places use the 'assert cond, ValueError(msg)' idiom, which raises AssertionError (the ValueError instance is just the assert message) and is silently DISABLED under python -O: (1) Normalize fitter min>=max -- its docstring explicitly documents 'Raises ValueError If min >= max'; (2) Smooth negative kernel_width; (3) tools.normalize's mode validation, whose message also references 'scale_type', a parameter name that does not exist in the 1.0 API (the kwarg is 'normalize='), e.g. hyp.normalize(x, normalize='banana') -> "AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer."
findings.expected: ValueError (as documented), raised unconditionally, with the message naming the actual parameter ('normalize').
findings.actual:
AssertionError minimum must be strictly less than maximum
AssertionError scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: Dict spec with an unknown model name leaks 'AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'fit_transform''
findings.description: manip(df, model='Foo') gives the excellent 'unknown manip model' ValueError, but the DICT form manip(df, model={'model': 'Bar', 'kwargs': {}}) leaks the unresolved string through _resolve_single_step's dict branch (cls stays the string 'Bar', then .fit_transform is called on it).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3)), model={'model': 'Bar', 'kwargs': {}})
findings.expected: The same clear ValueError as the bare-string path: "unknown manip model 'Bar'; supported names: Normalize, ZScore, Smooth, Resample ..."

findings.title: Invalid legacy mode= value is silently accepted (falls back to savgol); kernel= validates but mode= does not
findings.description: Smooth(kernel='hann') raises a clear ValueError listing the supported kernels, but the legacy Smooth(mode='hann') runs without any warning or error -- _resolve_kernel only checks mode == 'gaussian' and otherwise silently uses savgol. A user typo like mode='guassian' silently produces savgol smoothing instead of gaussian, changing results without notice.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
r = hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3)), model='Smooth', mode='hann')
print(type(r))  # DataFrame -- no error, silently savgol
findings.expected: ValueError (or at least a warning) for mode values outside {'savgol', 'gaussian'}.

findings.title: Row-wise (axis=1) fitted ZScore/Normalize silently transform NEW data using fit-time per-row statistics
findings.description: The inverters explicitly refuse axis=1 on the grounds that 'inverting a row-wise z-score on held-out data is ill-defined', yet the FORWARD transform of held-out data with a fitted axis=1 model is allowed and silently applies the fit-time per-ROW baselines/stats positionally to the new data's rows -- equally ill-defined. A Normalize(axis=1) fitted on (30,3) data transformed a (30,5) frame with no error (per-row params broadcast across the new row length). Expected either re-derivation per row (matching normalize()'s self-referential 'row' mode) or the same NotImplementedError the inverse raises.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 3), columns=list('abc'))
_, m = hyp.manip(df, model='Normalize', axis=1, return_model=True)
out = hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(30, 5)), model=m)
print(out.shape)  # (30, 5), silently used fit-time per-row baseline/peak
findings.expected: Error or per-row re-derivation; not silent reuse of fit-time row statistics on unrelated rows.

findings.title: manip is described as 'per-dataset' but ZScore/Normalize/Smooth fit ONE shared set of statistics across a list of datasets
findings.description: manip()'s docstring opens with 'Apply a per-dataset manipulation' and docs/pipeline_order.rst says 'Manip runs in native (per-dataset) space ... per-dataset preprocessing steps'. But for list input, the ZScore/Normalize/Smooth fitters concatenate all datasets ('one shared mean/std across all of them' -- documented only in the fitters) so manip(list, 'ZScore') is 'across'-list z-scoring: verified ds of 0s and ds of 1s z-score to about -1/+1, not to per-dataset 0s. There is no manip-level way to request within-dataset statistics for a list. The user-facing docs should state the shared-statistics semantics (and the Smooth cross-boundary behavior, finding 001, if it is not fixed).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
z = hyp.manip([np.zeros((30, 2)), np.ones((30, 2))], model='ZScore')
print(np.asarray(z[0], dtype=float)[:2, 0])
findings.expected: Docs matching behavior: per-dataset wording implies each dataset z-scored by its own stats (0s here).
findings.actual: ZScore list: ds0 values (shared stats -> approx -1): [-0.99163165 -0.99163165]

findings.title: normalize() docstring says 'If the input was a list, a list is returned' -- false for single-element lists
findings.description: hyp.normalize([A]) returns a bare ndarray, not a 1-element list (tools/normalize.py: 'if internal or len(normalized_x) > 1' unwraps single-element results). hyp.manip([A]) returns a 1-element list, so the two APIs also disagree. Long-standing classic behavior, but the Returns section is wrong as written.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(type(hyp.normalize([np.random.randn(10, 3)])))
findings.expected: list (per docstring), or a docstring documenting the single-element unwrap.

findings.title: hyp.manip('ZScore') and hyp.normalize() z-score with DIFFERENT std conventions (ddof=1 vs ddof=0) -- same data, different numbers
findings.description: manip ZScore's fitter uses pandas .std() (sample std, ddof=1); tools.normalize's Normalizer uses np.std (population std, ddof=0). On a 4-row matrix the same data z-scored by the two functions differs by sqrt(n/(n-1)) ~ 15% (manip output has population std 0.866; normalize output has population std 1.0). Neither docstring states which convention is used, and nothing warns that the library's two z-scoring entry points disagree. Scientists switching between hyp.normalize(x) and hyp.manip(x, 'ZScore') (or comparing against scipy.stats.zscore, ddof=0) get silently different values.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
H = np.array([[1., 0.], [2., 10.], [3., 20.], [4., 30.]])
print(np.asarray(hyp.manip(H, model='ZScore'), dtype=float).std(0, ddof=0))  # [0.866 0.866]
print(hyp.normalize(H, normalize='within').std(0, ddof=0))                   # [1. 1.]
findings.expected: One documented convention (or an explicit ddof parameter); docstrings stating which std is used.
findings.actual: manip ZScore axis=0: popstd=[0.8660254 0.8660254], sampstd=[1. 1.]; consistency manip-ZScore vs normalize-within: allclose = False

findings.title: Cross-API inconsistencies between manip() and normalize(): return types, DataFrame metadata, NaN handling, 1-D orientation
findings.description: For identical input the two preprocessing entry points behave differently on several axes: (1) manip(array) returns a pandas DataFrame while normalize(array) returns an ndarray; (2) normalize(DataFrame) DISCARDS index/columns (returns ndarray) while manip preserves them (including MultiIndexes); (3) normalize PPCA-imputes NaNs at format time while manip silently propagates NaN; (4) 1-D input is a row (1,n) to manip but a column (n,1) to normalize (see finding 006); (5) manip([A]) -> list but normalize([A]) -> array (finding 014). Each behavior is individually defensible; jointly they make the 'unified interface' claim leaky. At minimum the differences should be documented in both docstrings.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(10, 3), columns=list('abc'))
print(type(hyp.manip(df, model='ZScore')))   # DataFrame, metadata kept
print(type(hyp.normalize(df)))               # ndarray, metadata lost
findings.expected: Consistent (or explicitly documented) conventions across the two functions.
findings.actual: manip -> DataFrame (index/columns preserved, NaN propagated); normalize -> ndarray (metadata lost, NaN imputed)

findings.title: The 'unknown manip model' error recommends the DEPRECATED dict form
findings.description: manip's otherwise-excellent unknown-model ValueError tells users to 'pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}' -- the LEGACY form that itself emits a DeprecationWarning when used. It should recommend the canonical {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} form.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
hyp.manip(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(5, 2)), model='Foo')
findings.expected: Error text recommending the canonical dict form.
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown manip model 'Foo'; supported names: Normalize, ZScore, Smooth, Resample (or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, a Manipulator subclass, or a Manipulator instance directly)

findings.title: Several common data problems surface as raw scipy/numpy internals with no hypertools context
findings.description: Error-message quality gaps (each verified): (1) Resample on a duplicate or non-monotonic index -> 'ValueError: `x` must be strictly increasing sequence.' (scipy pchip; does not say Resample uses the DataFrame index or suggest reset_index / sorting); (2) Resample n_samples=10.5 -> 'TypeError: 'float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer' (numpy linspace, no parameter name); (3) normalize 'across' with datasets of different column counts -> raw numpy concatenate message ('all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 3 and the array at index 1 has size 4'). The Smooth kernel_width errors show the project's own good standard ('use a kernel_width <= 5'); these paths fall short of it.
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, hypertools as hyp
dup = pd.DataFrame({'y': [1., 2., 3., 4.]}, index=[0, 1, 1, 2])
hyp.manip(dup, model='Resample', n_samples=8)
findings.expected: Errors naming the offending hypertools parameter/data property and how to fix it.
findings.actual: ValueError: `x` must be strictly increasing sequence.

findings.title: No runnable Examples section in any manip/normalize public docstring
findings.description: Neither hyp.manip, hyp.normalize, nor any of the four Manipulator classes has a '>>>' Examples section (grep for '>>>' across hypertools/manip/ and tools/normalize.py returns nothing), so docs pages built via autofunction (docs/hypertools.manip.rst, docs/api.rst) render parameter tables with no copy-pasteable usage, and there are no doctests guarding these APIs. The embedded prose spec examples in manip()'s docstring do all work (verified: list/dict specs, ['Smooth','UMAP'], ['Smooth','HyperAlign']).
findings.expected: At least one runnable example per public function/class, doctest-checked.
findings.actual: grep returns no matches (verified during source review).
